otherSurfaces.whyNot: Closed behind a separate partner-program application, not self-serve.

oauthFit.reason: Standard authorization_code flow, but only three scopes (profile, email, w_member_social) are self-serve — everything else requires a separate partner-program application.

decision.question: Do you only need basic sign-in/sharing, or deeper LinkedIn data (ads, sales, talent)?

options.name: Open permissions (self-serve)
pickWhen: You only need Sign In with LinkedIn (profile, email)
You only need to post/comment/like on a member's behalf (Share on LinkedIn)
options.tradeoff: Instant, no approval — but limited to basic auth and posting. No access to connections, feed data, company data, ads, or sales data.

options.name: Partner program (Marketing / Sales Navigator / Talent)
pickWhen: You need Sales Navigator Application Platform (SNAP) access
You need a Talent Solutions integration (recruiting, job posting)
options.tradeoff: Requires applying to a separate partner program per product line — LinkedIn doesn't publish a review timeline, and each program has its own approval process.

decision.recommendation: If the integration only needs to sign users in or post on their behalf, stick to the open permissions — it's the only path that doesn't require an approval process.

summary: LinkedIn only self-serves three scopes: basic sign-in and posting on a member's behalf. Everything else — ad data, Sales Navigator, recruiting integrations — is closed behind a separate partner-program application per product line, each requiring LinkedIn's approval.

evidence.note: Official docs don't state a hands-on setup time for the open-permissions path; the estimate above is based on step count, not a documented figure.

paths.name: Open Permissions (Sign In with LinkedIn, Share on LinkedIn)
paths.notes: The only scopes available to all developers without approval.

paths.name: Marketing / Sales Navigator / Talent (partner programs)
paths.wait: No review timeline is published — each program has its own separate approval process
paths.notes: Each product line requires applying to and being approved by its own separate partner program.

cost.value: Open Permissions (Sign In with LinkedIn, Share on LinkedIn) are free with no per-call pricing. Marketing, Sales Navigator, and Talent products are gated behind separate partner-program approval rather than simple pay-per-call pricing — access is the gate, not a price list.
cost.notes: No stated usage cap for Open Permissions scopes in the docs reviewed. Commercial terms for partner-program products aren't detailed on the pages reviewed.

rateLimits.value: No published per-call rate limits for Open Permissions scopes in the docs reviewed.

evidence.note: Checked the authentication and getting-access docs; neither states a rate limit for Open Permissions.

prerequisites.text: A LinkedIn account and an app created in the Developer Portal.
An absolute HTTPS redirect URL to register under the app's Auth tab.

minimum.why: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect — basic identity, self-serve.

optional.why: Post/comment/like on a member's behalf — self-serve under Share on LinkedIn.

steps.title: Create a Developer Portal app
steps.description: Go to linkedin.com/developers/apps and create a new application.
steps.agentAssist: Can pre-fill the app name once a session is authenticated.

steps.title: Add an Open Permissions product
steps.description: Under the app's Products tab, add 'Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' (for the profile/email scopes) and/or 'Share on LinkedIn' (for the w_member_social scope). Both are self-serve — no approval needed.
steps.agentAssist: Can select the needed Open Permissions products directly.

steps.title: Configure the redirect URL
steps.description: Under the Auth tab, add an absolute HTTPS redirect URL (e.g. https://yourapp.com/auth/linkedin/callback). URLs with a # fragment are invalid; query parameters are ignored for matching.
steps.agentAssist: Can pre-fill Composio's redirect URI directly.

steps.title: Apply for partner-program products if more access is needed
steps.description: For Marketing/Advertising, Sales Navigator, or Talent Solutions data, apply separately for each product line under the Products tab — each requires LinkedIn's approval.
steps.agentAssist: Can draft the use-case and justification text for the application.

blockers.fix: The redirect URI sent in the request must exactly match the one registered under the Auth tab — it must be absolute HTTPS with no # fragment.

blockers.problem: Access tokens stop silently refreshing and users get sent through full re-authorization unexpectedly.
blockers.fix: Programmatic refresh tokens are only available to a limited set of approved partners. For everyone else, 'refreshing' works by silently re-running the auth flow while the member is still logged into linkedin.com with a non-expired token — if either condition isn't met, they go through the full consent screen again.

blockers.problem: All previously issued tokens stop working after a scope change.
blockers.fix: If the app's requested scopes change, every token issued under the old scope set is invalidated — all users must re-authenticate, not just new ones.

agentCanDo: Find the Developer Portal app-creation form and its current fields
Pre-fill the app name, redirect URL, and Open Permissions products to add
Draft the partner-program application text — use case, requested scopes, and justification — for Marketing, Sales Navigator, or Talent access
humanMustDo: Create the app in the LinkedIn Developer Portal
Add Open Permissions products, or apply for partner programs, under the Products tab
Configure the redirect URL under the Auth tab
Apply separately to each partner program (Marketing/Sales/Talent) if deeper access is needed
composioHandoff: Paste the client ID and client secret into Composio, with Composio's callback URL registered as the app's redirect URL — Composio manages the authorization flow, token exchange, and refresh from there.
openQuestions: LinkedIn doesn't publish a review timeline for partner-program applications (Marketing/Advertising, Sales Navigator, Talent) on the pages reviewed — budget for an unpredictable wait.
Exact application requirements per partner program (e.g. whether a privacy policy or product demo must be submitted) aren't detailed on the official pages reviewed.
Whether a non-partner app can ever gain Sales Navigator or Talent access outside the formal partner programs.
